programs.desc: ECHO is continuing to build a knowledge base of agricultural practices and appropriate technologies and then deliver this knowledge to development workers around the globe to reduce hunger and improve the livelihoods of small-scale farmers. The thousands of users and hundreds of organizations who utilize ECHO resources regularly evaluate the usefulness and impact of these resources and the effectiveness of their delivery.

The work of the Regional Impact Centers/Teams is heavily supported by ECHO's U.S.-based activities identified in 4a above. ECHO's regional resources and trainings are regularly evaluated by practitioners throughout the regions.

In FY 2024-25, the Seattle cohort completed their first year of the program with a one-week in-person retreat in Sept 2024 and Feb 2025 with 45 students. The Omaha cohort completed its second year of the program with a one-week in-person retreat in Nov 2024 and June 2025 with 42 students.

Conferences and retreats are planned and facilitated to encourage people to practice a meaningful spiritual life. In April 2025 the annual pastor's retreat, "First Love", was held for 43 pastors and ministry leaders. In June 2025, Renovare held its second biennial event, "The ReGathering," a 3-day event that is "part conference, part retreat, and part family reunion." It was attended in-person by approximately 370 people.

Spiritual Formation education is a core of Renovare's ministry and remained an emphasis for FY 2024-25. This general education occurs through various platforms: such as podcasts via the website (renovare.org), the online Renovare book club with a record 2100 participants, and various speaking engagements. Renovare has continued webinars that were created in response to limited in-person gatherings. Three webinars were hosted in FY2024-25, with an average webinar having over 1,000 registrations. Renovare also hosted two online workshops - one on the art of kintsugi, and the other focused on how to hear God. Renovare continues to see people register for their free "From the Inside Out" online course. Over 9,300 people from 120 countries have registered for the course, podcast episodes were downloaded over 230,000 times and over 41,000 people now receive the "Renovare Weekly" email each Fri

To support renewal at a congregational level, Renovare offers resources and experiences for churches through its Churches in Renewal initiative. These include the Churches in Renewal Cohort Learning Experience (CIRCLE), participation at the annual pastors retreat, and other content and community life offerings. CIRCLE is an immersive ten-month program of study, prayer, and interchurch dialogue. In FY2024-25, seven Atlanta churches participated in CIRCLE. Three to five individuals from each church (total of 30 people) participated in the program. Cohort-wide in-person meetings were held on October 14, 2024, January 10, 2025, March 17, 2025 and May 9, 2025.

411897793.mission: To provide healing and hope to victims of domestic abuse through supportive services and a safe, transitional place to call home.

programs.desc: Transitional Housing - The Organization operates ten single-family homes that provide transitional housing for women and children fleeing domestic abuse. Residents typically remain in the program for two years while they recover from trauma and develop the skills necessary to achieve independent housing, sustainable income, and lives free from abuse. The homes are located in residential neighborhoods, and their locations are kept confidential to protect the safety of the women and children served. The properties include 40 bedrooms and can accommodate up to 80 individuals. The homes are furnished, well maintained, and equipped with security systems. In 2025, the Organization housed and served 24 women and 34 children, ranging in age from 8 months to 17 years. A total of 58 women and children received 12,645 nights of safe housing. The Organization also received 660 calls for assistance i

Community Education - The Organization provides trauma-informed care focused on two primary principles: safety and empowerment. With more than 27 years of experience serving victims of domestic abuse, the Organization integrates best practices in trauma-informed care within a Christ-centered environment. The Organization provides a comprehensive program of support services for residents, including intensive case management, support groups, education on domestic abuse, financial literacy and budgeting classes, parenting education, music, art and talk therapy, and instruction on meal planning and nutrition on a limited budget. Bible study and Christian spiritual support are also available. The Organization collaborates with community partners to provide additional resources, including employment counseling, therapy services, and assistance with securing affordable housing.

Residential Program- Because all of the residents are single mothers, the Organization also provides programming and support services for their children. Children residing in the homes receive case management, access to mental and behavioral health services, individual trauma therapy, and age-appropriate educational support. Mothers in the program receive individualized parenting support and education designed to help them meet the developmental and emotional needs of their children and access appropriate community services. The Children's Program focuses on promoting healing from trauma and supporting development in social, emotional, and cognitive skills, while strengthening the relationship between mothers and their children. The children are also offered one-on-one tutoring, and specialized kid's support group after school.

Alumni Program - The Organization maintains an Alumni Program to support residents who have transitioned out of the residential program and to monitor long-term outcomes. The program provides continued support through mentorship, monthly case management, support groups, and periodic community-building activities.

593735653.mission: We rescue, love and care for orphans and impoverished children in Haiti, meeting their physical, emotional, educational and spiritual needs so they are empowered to become leaders in their communities and nation.

programs.desc: The Medical + Malnutrition Center served over 7,800 patients via emergency care, intake/assessment, diagnostic blood analysis, radiology lab, outpatient treatment, inpatient treatment for malnutrition, pharmacy and medical transport to and from the Center. The Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) treated 303 patients. The Dental Clinic served 1,298 patients with dental hygiene, preventative and restorative services, along with supplies. Wellness education was given on disease prevention/wellness. Near death children were saved from starvation through an inpatient nutrition and medical regimen with an outpatient program to ensure wellness and to monitor patients' food security. Our Malnutrition Mountain Outreach Program treated 2,283 children who live in rural areas without access to medical care.

The Children's Homes provided full-time care for 48 orphans in 6 independently operating households which include a House Parent for 12 to 15 children, one for children with special needs. This provides a nurturing family-type setting with safe, comfortable rooms, nourishing food (3 meals per day), clothing (including school uniforms), and emotional and spiritual care/support. There are three trained nurses who provide 24/7 specialized nursing care to each child and house moms provide care to these children, treating each one of them with the utmost dignity, respect, and love. This home provided 12 children with special needs and physical disabilities with care. These children are often discarded by their families and society.

The School educated 370 students, preschool through Grade 13, including 33 children from the Children's Homes and nearby Ouanaminthe. The School has 17 classrooms and employs almost 40 Haitians, providing supplies, books, uniforms and medical care. A feeding program began in 2002 when children would come to school hungry, unable to focus. Curriculum follows Haiti's Ministry of Education and U.S. based strategies for analytical reasoning and problem-solving. Students learn 4 languages. The sports program allows students to compete in sports such as soccer and volleyball. Since 2014, 97 students out of 98 have graduated High School and received support and guidance through the Scholarship Program with 15 attending college/vocational school in Haiti and 4 attending college in the U.S.

Approximately 500 people from the community attend Temple de l'Espoir, a church operated by the organization on its campus each week. The church hosts conferences and events open to the community for spiritual enrichment. The farm is located on 106 acres of land outside of Ouanaminthe. The farming project currently consists of peanuts, sugar cane, pineapple, banana trees, plantain trees and yuca plants. The next phase is developing a goat and chicken farm. The goal of this program is to become more self-sustainable. This project will supplement our feeding program, ensuring that we can provide nutritious food for the children who come to us for help.

473518333.mission: DC127s mission is to strengthen and stabilize families impacted by the foster care system in Washington, DC, by mobilizing the Church to provide wraparound support.

programs.desc: Communities for families (CFF): The Communities for Families program works to keep children out of foster care by identifying and mitigating risk factors, ultimately strengthening families and helping them stay together. DC127 trains volunteers to provide holistic support to preserve families who have one or more risk factors that may increase their potential for family disruption, leading to a child(ren) experiencing foster care. This volunteer-supported effort removes barriers to healthy parenting, decreases feelings of isolation, provides access to resources and life skills training, and ultimately creates stronger parents and safer homes for children.

Church mobilization: DC127 partners with local churches to mobilize volunteers to directly support families at risk of separation, as well as foster and kinship families in the tools, resources, and relationships they need to come alongside families in their own communities, with the goal of strengthening families and disrupting the pathways that lead to foster care.

Foster care support: The Foster Care Support program exists to strengthen foster and kinship families while they provide stability and support for children in their care. Through education, community connection, and practical resources, DC127 creates a welcoming space for individuals to learn about foster care in Washington, DC and explore becoming a licensed foster home. In partnership with the Child and Family Services Agency, DC127 recruits and supports DC foster and kinship parents, ensuring families are surrounded by a caring community as they care for some of DCs most vulnerable children.

203596433.mission: Treasures mission is to reach, restore, and equip women in the sex industry and victims of sex trafficking to live healthy, flourishing lives, and train others to do the same across the globe.

programs.desc: Through our survivor-led mentoring, support groups, emergency relief fund, gentle case management and community partnerships, Treasures helps women who have experienced exploitation and trafficking heal from their past and rebuild their lives. Weekly Online Support Groups: a safe place where women can experience peer support, skill building and healing. Mentoring: Women are matched with a mentor to help them process their current life circumstances. Coaching: A 6-week program designed to empower women in goal setting. Case Management: We help women access residential programs, vocational and educational training, legal assistance, funding through victims of crime and more. Financial Assistance: to help women overcome the harsh realities of poverty, unemployment and homelessness.

Our outreach efforts are focused on strip clubs, juvenile detention centers, the porn industry and online forums where women and girls are exploited and solicited for sex. Each year, Treasures reaches 5,000 women working in strip clubs and the porn industry in Los Angeles and Las Vegas. We give them gift bags filled with cosmetics, jewelry and the simple message that they are loved, valued and purposed, and that support is available to them. We bring this same message of hope to commercially sexually exploited children CSEC during our outreaches in juvenile detention centers, as well as in online forums, and to an HIV testing center for women in porn. Furthermore, we provide training and mentoring to leaders across the globe in order to equip them to develop sex industry outreaches in their community. We have helped train and launch more than 100 sex industry outreaches on 6 continents.

383934583.mission: Serve the Bachman Lake Community with quality faith-based programs targeting specific community needs, starting with education of parents and children, emotional well-being and material needs.

programs.desc: Elementary School Literacy Program - There are 2 parts to the elementary school literacy program. The first is the After School Reading program, which began in the fall of 2018. This program provides reading intervention for low-income students. The second part of the elementary school literacy program is Summer at the Lake. This summer reading enrichment program for K-5th graders uses trained teenagers as literacy counselors. The program's goal is to help underserved elementary students in Bachman Lake maintain or improve their reading proficiency over the summer. The teen counselors receive leadership and literacy training to run the camps.

Early Childhood Education Program - Serves low income Hispanic children from Bachman Lake Community with early education classes. This program focuses on language acquisition, pre-math skills, gross and fine motor development, social skills development, and executive function. Parent workshops focus on child development, parent talk (3Ts from thirty million words initiative), play with me, every child ready to read, emotional development, disciplining your child, sleep patterns, and children's health. Each workshop includes practical hands-on applications so that parents and children learn skills together and are equipped to practice these skills at home. Program has a student-to-teacher ratio which allows for individualized attention to each student. Each student's progress is evaluated at the beginning and end of each school year.

Adult Education Program - Provides classes in English, computer literacy, and financial literacy for low income Hispanic adults from the Bachman Lake Community. Over 70% of students who complete the year advance to the next level, which means they have made significant progress in reading, speaking, and writing in English. Students in our classes also receive regular workshops on life skills and such as cultural assimilation, language learning, financial literacy, health, nutrition, depression, grief, family dynamics, school choice, internet safety, and child development. The Bible and prayer are incorporated into all aspects of the program and students are invited, but not forced, to participate in faith-based activities.

programs.desc: Children, youth and family programs: City On A Hill provides holistic support to low-income families, children and youth, empowering them to break the cycle of poverty. We engage hundres of youth annually in growth-focused activities like after school programs, summer initiatives and experiential learning opportunities. We also offer family services including home visits, emergency assistance, caregive support groups and community-building events, all designed to foster strong families and vibrant communities.

Healthcare services: City On A Hill delivers life-changing healthcare services to over 1,000 economically disadvantaged individuals annually, including those experiencing homelessness, the elderly and people with disabilities. Our comprehensive care includes health screenings, physician consultations, medication provision, teleheath access, vision care, rehabilitative services, diabetes prevention and cancer screenings. Our specialized initiative for those in shelters and transitional housing emphasizes health education and system navigation, ensureing that all can access dignified, no-cost primary care.

911148123.mission: The mission of Mercy Corps is to alleviate suffering, poverty, and oppression by helping people build secure, productive, and just communities.

programs.desc: Economic Opportunities: Mercy Corps helps increase economic opportunities and ensures people can grow and sustain their assets and income, making markets more efficient, profitable and accessible for systemically marginalized groups and those living in poverty. To increase economic opportunity, Mercy Corps strengthens financial ecosystems, develops tech-enabled solutions, facilitates the creation of and access to jobs that are profitable, dignified, and safe, and foster opportunities for sustainable and productive economic growth that mitigates the impact of climate change. This year, Mercy Corps reached over 19 million people through over 130 programs across 38 countries working to increase economic opportunity.

Humanitarian Assistance - relief: Mercy Corps helps people most impacted by conflict and climate change cope, adapt and thrive, supporting millions facing natural and man-made disasters by providing support such as food, clean water, shelter and basic hygiene to help them cope in the midst of conflict, natural disasters and weather-related incidents. Mercy Corps helps communities prepare for and respond to humanitarian needs as they arise, while supporting recovery and laying the foundations for resilience even in the most extreme humanitarian situations. This year, Mercy Corps provided humanitarian assistance to millions facing acute and protracted emergencies around the world, including in Sudan, Gaza, Haiti - reaching 37.6 million people across programs.

Peace and good governance (Civil society and education): Mercy Corps supports people and communities to reduce and prevent violence, contribute to advancing sustainable peace, and participating meaningfully in civil society and inclusive and responsive governance systems. By sequencing, layering, and integrating our peace, humanitarian, and development assistance, we help advance peace and promote inclusive, responsive governance processes, that enable communities - and the most marginalized within them - to cope, adapt, and thrive. This year, Mercy Corps reached over 14 million people with peace and good governance programs across 29 countries.

Humanitarian Assistance - Recovery: Mercy Corps supports communities - and the most marginalized within them - to emerge from crisis and build towards a more inclusive, resilient future. During and in the aftermath of conflict and climate-driven crises, Mercy Corps works to help people recover, thrive and build resilience, enhancing the capacities of people, markets, and institutions to handle shocks, reduce risk, build more equitable and responsive systems, and improve wellbeing. In the context of post-crisis recovery, we focus on systems-level change aimed at strengthening local governance, economic, ecological, and social systems that communities rely on.

IN 1919, A FUNDRAISING CAMPAIGN RESULTED IN 83,000 RESIDENTS CONTRIBUTING $2.5 MILLION IN 10 DAYS (MORE THAN $45 MILLION IN CURRENT DOLLARS). IN 1921, A SITE DEDICATION HOSTED MORE THAN 100,000 PEOPLE, INCLUDING THE FIVE MAJOR ALLIED COMMANDERS THE FIRST TIME THESE INDIVIDUALS WERE IN THE SAME PLACE AT THE SAME TIME. FOLLOWING YEARS OF PLANNING AND CONSTRUCTION, THE MEMORIAL OPENED IN 1926 TO A CROWD OF MORE THAN 150,000 PEOPLE, INCLUDING U.S. PRESIDENT CALVIN COOLIDGE. AT THE TIME, IT WAS THE LARGEST AUDIENCE A U.S. PRESIDENT HAD EVER ADDRESSED AT ONE TIME. AFTER DECADES OF UNADDRESSED DEFERRED MAINTENANCE, THE MEMORIAL TEMPORARILY CLOSED IN 1994. 710407333.mission: To provide basic, secondary, and college education to over 1,000 students in the country of Zambia; to provide needy student scholarships, orphans' care, medical care, and conduct health clinics in remote areas to teach better hygiene, and protection against HIV/AIDS and malaria; and to drill water wells to provide clean drinking water to the people in Zambia, Africa

programs.desc: CLINIC/MEDICINE/MEDICAL OUTREACHES AND ORPHANS CARE A medical hospital has been built at the Mission to serve the Mission, schools, and villages in the area. For many years a group of medical doctors, dentists, eye doctors, nurses, and lay persons from the USA have traveled to Zambia at their own expense to conduct medical clinics in the bush and villages; in a typical year, about 75 from the US join about 150 Zambian volunteers. Hospitals are few and far between in Zambia and most of the people cannot go to a doctor for medical treatment. Between 7,500 and 15,000 Zambians are treated by medical personnel during this short time period. This is a service program and no revenue is received.ORPHANS CARE Because of malaria and HIV/AIDS, there are thousands and thousands of orphans in Zambia. Large homes have been built at the Mission to care for some of these orphans. The need is so great an

EDUCATION AND NEEDY STUDENT SCHOLARSHIP PROGRAM Most of our students are from the bush or villages in Zambia. They are very poor and many of them are orphans and live with extended family members who have no money for their education. The Needy Student Scholarship Program provides all their school fees (room, board, and tuition). Because education is so valued in this Third World Country, these students have proven to do very well. They study hard and are grateful for the opportunity to go to school. This is a service program and no revenue is received.

CLEAN WATER PROJECTS/CONSTRUCTION/EQUIPMENT/VEHICLES One of the many needs in Zambia is available clean drinking water. Several deep water wells have been drilled and equipped with pumps in some of the villages. Purification facilities and storage tanks have been constructed to purify and store water from lakes in the area. New dorms for secondary and college students have been constructed and others have been remodeled. Classrooms and the cafeteria have been remodeled. These are service projects to better serve the students and people in the villages and no revenue is received.

561366233.mission: SEEKING TO PUT GOD'S LOVE INTO ACTION, HABITAT FOR HUMANITY BRINGS PEOPLE TOGETHER TO BUILD HOMES, COMMUNITIES, AND HOPE.

programs.desc: Habitat Charlotte Region has been the leading provider of affordable homeownership and home repair solutions since 1983, serving families earning 80% or less of the Area Median Income. We operate in Gaston, Iredell, North Mecklenburg, and the cities of Charlotte, and Pineville, supporting a region of over 1.5 million people. In FY 25 we partnered with 197 families through affordable housing solutions and with more than 350 on financial education. In October 2024, we merged with Habitat for Humanity of Gaston County, combining our individual effort to strengthen affordable housing across the region. This merger expands impact, maximizes resources, and increases affordable homeownership opportunities. Our mission is to promote affordable homeownership as a path to financial stability and economic mobility. We achieve this through three programs: *Critical Home Repair - Providing repairs th

Our mission is sustained through a healthy mix of funding streams to support our operating needs, growth goals and strategic plan. 7 ReStores, where we sell new and gently-used furniture, appliances, home decor, and building materials support our operational expenses. Donations from individuals, corporations, foundations and faith partners remain a strong financial resource for Habitat Charlotte Region, and public grants continue to enable us to scale our programs and pilot new programs. This year, we also launched a $20M capacity building campaign and confirmed the first $5M in commitments. Habitat Charlotte Region understands the effects of homeownership on asset-building and wealth, and is committed to serving the community while recognizing that change and adaptability are key to intensifying our impact. Next year we are launching 2 co-developed, mixed income, light-density projects

Our Critical Home Repair program provides qualified families with significant home repairs, improving substandard housing conditions for those with limited financial resources and preserving affordable units in our community. Our team focuses on four essential health and safety issues: unsafe roofs or floors, lacking heat, electrical system hazards, and plumbing hazards while also addressing accessibility issues in and around the home. 197 families were served through this program during the year.

Building on the success of Money Matters, a financial literacy course focused on helping individuals become homebuyer ready, Habitat Charlotte Region expanded its financial literacy programming to offer three pathways depending on an individual's financial readiness. This approach allows us to provide a more customized experience and timeline based on an initial financial assessment. Through the expanded financial literacy program, now called Pathways and Partners, the affiliate helped 350 families. During the year, Habitat Charlotte Region provided support to Habitat for Humanity International.

The hospital operations of Rush University Medical Center are licensed by the State of Illinois to operate 678 beds and include the Johnston R. Bowman Health Center, which provides medical and rehabilitative care to older adults and people with short- and long-term disabilities, and Rush University Children's Hospital. According to COMPdata, RUMC is the fifth largest hospital provider in the eight county Chicago metropolitan area as measured by market share. It also includes a faculty practice plan, Rush University Medical Group, which employs more than 700 physicians and 300 advanced practice providers in more than 111 specialties and subspecialties, singularly focused on transforming health care and providing ex

Research: Because Rush is an academic medical center, research and clinical care come together in innovative and inspiring ways that have the power to transform lives. Even if research work starts in a laboratory, it won't stay there. Discoveries in Rush's labs lead to advances in patient care, while observations in clinical settings inspire research studies designed to improve the way we treat patients. This approach, known as translational research, has led to breakthroughs in patient care at Rush throughout the years. Investigators at Rush are involved in more than 500 projects, including hundreds of clinical studies to test the effectiveness and safety of new therapies and medical devices, as well as to expand scientific and medical knowledge. Total research awards in FY2024 topped $113 million.

Education: Rush University (RU) is a health sciences university that includes Rush Medical College, the College of Nursing, and the College of Health Sciences. Founded in 1837, Rush Medical College has an acclaimed history as one of the first medical colleges in the Midwest and continues to make major contributions to medical science and education through research and clinical trials. The College of Nursing is one of the nation's top-ranked nursing colleges with a national reputation for clinical excellence that helps make our graduates highly sought after by top health care employers around the country. The College of Health Sciences has been responsible for education and research in the allied health professions. The Medical Center also offers many highly selective residency and fellowship programs in medical and surgical specialties and subspecialties. RU's unique practitioner-teacher

Other program services: Rush provides various services for the benefit of its patients and visitors, such as parking, food services and interpreter services. Rush also sponsors a number of programs in the community focused on improving health, expanding education in health-related careers, community-based research to reduce health disparities and initiatives to provide economic development and job creation. Rush programs influenced tens of thousands of lives in FY2024.

programs.desc: Healthy Living: The Y is a leading voice on health and well-being. We bring families closer together, encourage good health and foster connections through fitness, sports, fun and shared interests. We provide guidance and resources they need to achieve greater health in spirit, mind and body. This is particular important as our nation struggles with an obesity crisis, chronic diseases, families struggle with work/life balance and individuals search for personal fulfillment. Our programs are accessible, affordable and open to all faiths, backgrounds, abilities and income levels. This year we provided financial assistance to people who otherwise may not have been able to afford to participate.

Youth Development: Our YMCA is committed to nurturing the potential of every child and teen. We believe that all kids deserve the opportunity to discover who they are and what they can achieve. That's why we help young people cultivate the values, skills and relationships that lead to positive behaviors, better health and educational achievement. Our YMCA programs, such as Youth in Government, Y Reads mentoring and enrichment programs, academic enrichment and homework assistance, and literacy summer camps and wellness programs, offer a range of experiences that enrich cognitive, social, physical and emotional growth and wellness. Expenses include subsidies and direct financial assistance that make participation possible for the young people that we engage. To a large degree serving Title 1 schools and their students.

Social Responsibility: Our YMCA believes in giving back and supporting our neighbors. We have been listening and responding to our community's most critical social needs for multiple decades. Y programs, such as Meals for Hope, Klothes for Kids, senior lunches, bread runs, health lecture series and family functions are examples of how we deliver training, resources and support that empower our neighbors to effect change, bridge gaps and overcome obstacles. This year we engaged YMCA members, participants and volunteers in activities that strengthen our community and pave the way for future generations to survive.

The Collaborative provides a centralized source for access to resources needed to support research and development of Ataxia therapies. Specific objectives of the Collaborative include natural history and bio sample data collection, development of biomarkers, validation of rating scales, clinical trial design, patient-reported outcomes, and other data necessary for the development and approval of safe and effective therapies. 270647923.mission: Sacra Script Ministries is a Christian ministry who promotes Bible study learning. This includes the presentation of various courses and seminars as well as the production and distribution of Bible study materials.

programs.desc: Sacra Script Ministries continued development of the Bible Ventures app, which provides instructional resources designed to help users understand the historical and literary context of Scripture in English, Spanish and Chinese. During the year, the ministry produced and added new Bible Exhibits covering significant people, places, events, and themes related to the biblical narrative. The app now serves more than 70,000 users in four languages across multiple countries. The ministry also carried out translation work to expand access to its materials, including refining existing translations, preparing new translated content, and reviewing translated materials for accuracy. These activities supported the organization's mission by increasing the availability of Bible study resources for individuals and churches in the United States and internationally.

Sacra Script Ministries developed a new teaching series focused on the life and ministry of Jesus as recorded in the Gospels. During the year, the ministry produced and recorded 56 lessons for this series, providing structured instruction intended to help participants understand the chronology, context, and major themes of Jesus' life. More than 1,000 individuals attended and participated in the series through live sessions and recorded content. This work supported the organization's educational purpose by offering accessible, organized biblical instruction to individuals and churches.

Sacra Script Ministries developed a new Bible study series on the books of 1 Kings and 2 Kings in conjunction with Sacra Script's Bible Ventures app. During the year, the ministry taught the series live in order to produce a full video-based course and completed the first 20 lessons. Approximately 500 individuals attended and participated in the sessions. This work supports the organization's educational purpose by generating structured biblical instruction that will be used for ongoing training. All lesson materials from this series, as well as future series, will be developed into courses with written notes and prepared for translation into additional languages to increase accessibility for individuals and churches.

programs.desc: The CAC provides a multidisciplinary approach to the intervention, investigation, and prosecution of child abuse. No other agency in the community provides coordination of services for child abuse victims. CAC provides a consistent, non-threatening, developmentally appropriate approach to the forensic interviewing of children. Forensic interviewis allow a child to be interviewed once at which time the investigation team members gather information they need. This prevents repeated interviews by different individuals which can further traumatize a child. A client advocate shares resources with the non-offending caregivers to ensure that the family understands how to keep their children safe following an investigation as well as providing the family with information about community and government assistance available to them. The Center provides crisis intervention, hospital and judicial ac

Our Therapy Program includes a Therapy Director who provides full- time therapy and other full-time therapists. Services include teletherapy. The therapists and clients develop treatment goals and may utilize a variety of therapy approaches to meet individual needs and to promote health and healing. We continue the Thrive support group for adult victims of sexual abuse/assault and have a therapist led support group for male adult sexual assault victims.

Education of our community is very important to the goals of the Center. Two full-time staff are employed by the Center to provide education and training to the community. The education program provides a variety of presentations to schools and professionals. The presentations include Being Safe for kindergarten through 6th grade students. MRCCAC Education department currently presents internet safety to children and parents. Our Education Program provides presentations to teachers, parents, and community members in Midland, Martin, Howard, and Andrews county. Our agency hosts the Sexual Assault Response Team for adults in Midland County including Midland College. This team analyzes our community response to sexual assault. Recommendations are made for improvements.

programs.desc: Children's Garden is licensed by the Department of Social Welfare as a Residential Care facility providing housing and supplemental education to boys who had been living on the streets of Metro Manila. Many have been deemed to be In crisis with the Law and without facilities like Children's Garden they would be housed in the overcrowded municipal jails. Teachers and Social Workers working with Children's Garden enabled 17 of these boys to move up to the next grade level in Primary school and helped 7 boys complete Secondary school this past year. Many of the resident boys begin training in life skills and vocational skills while being mainstreamed into their primary grades in Public School. Having access to teachers, a library and classroom within Children's Garden allows most of the boys to catch up to their age group peers and graduate close to on-time.

The 2nd Phase program developed out of the need to reinforce and continue the success of Children's Garden. Young families and adults who were raised in the Children's Garden shelter and network continue to receive mentorship and guidance from our partners. Funding is provided for unexpected medical needs, disaster relief, continuing education, and certification and licensing requirements for employment. 1 young man received grants for building supplies to reinforce their concrete hollow block home and upgrade their plumbing. Weddings for three of the Children's Garden 'alum' were provided for. 4 individuals received assistance with expenses related to College or Vocational licensing.

At This Moment recognizes the conditions of the homeless in the neighborhoods we see everyday. Although the majority of our efforts are directed to homelessness and children in crisis with the law in the Philippines we are driven to care for the increasing number of families seen on the streets in the United States. Partnering with Homeward Bound and the Nevada Homeless Alliance we provided shelter and land access to more 154 individuals, 63 family clusters. Emergent medical needs were provided for 17 individuals. Access to portable hygiene stations was provided by the WASH Foundation. Food, laundry services and showers were provided for 110-130 unique recipients.

Migrant assistance evolved from working with the homeless in Southern Nevada. Individuals who had an option to live with extended family members were provided assistance. Costs were covered for: bedding, hygeine, clothing, building materials for room partitions, transportation and short-tern transitional housing. 11 families were provided for.

programs.desc: Mission Santa Maria is dedicated to helping impoverished, abused, and neglected Ecuadorian children receive high quality education. For over 17 years we have partnered with local organizations to create a santuary for children living in extreme poverty and vulnerability. We believe that alleviating poverty begins with faith and love and continues through education, conmbined with long-term challenge and support into professional and family life. 731393193.mission: To prevent child abuse and provide opportunities for healing and hope for children in Oklahoma County. The vision of The CARE Center is to end child abuse in Oklahoma County.

programs.desc: Child Advocacy Program: The CARE Center provides trauma-informed forensic interviews in a safe, child-focused environment where children can share their experiences of abuse. Trained interviewers conduct non-leading, recorded interviews while investigators observe from another room, reducing the number of times a child must retell their story and lowering the risk of re-traumatization. Family Advocates support each family through the investigation, prosecution, and healing process by helping them understand their rights and connect with needed resources. In 2024, the program conducted 1,122 forensic interviews and provided 3,015 advocacy services to children and their families.

Mental Health Services: The CARE Center provides children and families with on-site and virtual counseling, crisis intervention, observational assessments, mental health education, and referrals for long-term therapy through partner agencies. In 2024, our mental health team grew to three licensed therapists, including one bilingual Spanish-speaking therapist, along with a coordinator who helps families create individualized care plans. The program provided 1,139 therapy sessions and connected 365 children and families with external counseling resources

Prevention & Education Program: The CARE Center equips adults and children with the knowledge and tools to prevent abuse. Our free Recognizing & Reporting Child Abuse & Neglect training helps adults who work with children identify signs of abuse and understand their reporting responsibilities. Our ROAR program empowers children ages 4 to 8 to recognize unsafe situations and protect themselves. In 2024, we trained 1,017 adults and reached 25,374 children across the Oklahoma City metro community. Since the program began in 2017, more than 100,000 children have received ROAR safety education

Medical & Wellness: The CARE Center provides medical and wellness exams for children through our on-site clinic in partnership with a local children?s hospital. These exams evaluate and treat medical conditions resulting from abuse or neglect, ensure the child's well-being, and may collect evidence to support investigations. In 2024, the program conducted 117 medical exams and provided 228 medical consultations to children and their families
